chains.title: GABPA binds the alt allele and activates TERT

links.claim: GABPA is the leading ETS-family candidate: E04 lists GABPA among expressed TFs with a binding model found at this element in other biosamples, and E16 shows no GABPA peak in glioblastoma; no QBiC-SELEX model is available. The alt-A allele is inferred to bind GABPA more strongly because TERT is on the minus strand (E02), so the plus-strand G>A is a C>T change on the gene strand, the common TERT promoter mutation class (E15d), which is expected to create an ETS site; direct allele-specific occupancy is not shown.
E01 and E03 place the variant in the TERT promoter-like PLS EH38E3622530 with active chromatin marks; this supports promoter element localization, but not allele-specific activity.
TERT is the nearest gene at 0 kb (E02), and TERT promoter mutations of this class are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (E15d); this variant's direct effect on TERT is not demonstrated.
TERT promoter mutations and telomerase activation are established in melanoma and glioblastoma (E15a, E15d, E15g), making these disease contexts plausible.
Higher TERT/telomerase activity is associated with tumor progression in melanoma and glioblastoma (E15a, E15b, E15d, E15g); variant-specific causality is not shown.

chains.title: GABPA binds the alt allele but represses TERT

links.claim: GABPA is the leading ETS-family candidate and is inferred to bind the alt-A allele more strongly via the TERT promoter hotspot-like C>T change, but no QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific occupancy assay is available; E04 lists GABPA among expressed TFs with binding elsewhere and E16 confirms no glioblastoma GABPA peak.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter-like PLS EH38E3622530 with active chromatin marks (E01, E03), so it could mediate repressive as well as activating TF effects; this is not demonstrated.

TERT is the proximal target (E02); a masked cis SNP C allele has been associated with reduced TERT expression in TERT promoter-mutant glioblastoma (E15e), but this has not been shown for the present alt-A allele.

TERT promoter-mutant glioblastoma is a relevant context (E15d), and a cis variant has been linked to altered TERT expression and prognosis in that setting (E15e), but not specifically for this allele.

A masked cis SNP C allele with reduced TERT expression has been associated with poorer prognosis in TERT promoter-mutant glioblastoma (E15e), and TERT promoter status is prognostically relevant (E15g); this is not established for the present variant.

grades_v0.reason: No cited evidence shows GABPA binds the alt allele more strongly. E04 states no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context, so no peak counts as bound here; E05 is MAX, not GABPA; E01 only locates the variant. No QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific assay is provided.

E01 and E03 directly place the variant in a TERT promoter-like PLS cCRE with active chromatin marks. They do not show that this base alters promoter activity; that part remains indirect without reporter/MPRA/CRISPR evidence.

E02 supports TERT as the nearest gene at 0 kb, and E15d supports that TERT promoter mutations are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. It does not show this G>A variant is the oncogenic TERT promoter mutation or directly targets TERT.

E15a supports telomerase activation by TERT promoter mutations in melanoma; E15d supports frequency in glioblastoma but not activation in glioma cells. The combined cell-type claim is consistent but indirect.

The literature quotes support general TERT/telomerase relevance in melanoma and glioblastoma, but none is a variant-specific perturbation showing increased TERT expression from this allele or a causal progression effect.
Same binding problem as chain_1: no cited allele-specific GABPA occupancy and no QBiC-SELEX direction. E04 says no matching ENCODE biosample counts as bound; E05 is MAX, not GABPA.
E01/E03 support localization in a TERT promoter cCRE, but there is no evidence that this variant mediates repressive TF effects. The repression aspect is speculative.

E02 supports TERT proximity. E15e concerns a masked rs with a C allele and reduced TERT expression in TERT promoter-mutant glioblastoma; that is not clearly this G>A variant and does not establish repression for the alt A allele.
E15d/E15e support TERT promoter-mutant glioblastoma as a relevant context generally, but E15e is not clearly this variant and the repression direction is not demonstrated.

E15e reports an association between a masked cis SNP C allele, reduced TERT expression, and poorer prognosis, but this is not shown for the present G>A allele. E15g supports TPM frequency/prognostic relevance only generally.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
Mutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

The rs[masked] C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
Among 112 patients, 70 (62.5%) harbored TERTp mutations.
